per_question.answer: In these reports, employees exposed to ammonia leaks suffered breathing and swallowing difficulties, eye blurriness, and other respiratory problems that required hospitalization [2036538][2205704][1735357]. Several workers experienced chemical burns and skin irritation from the gas [1017209][2115614]. The exposure also caused unconsciousness and loss of consciousness in some cases [1017209][1735357]. Injuries to the lungs and eyes were noted when ammonia contacted the face or was inhaled [2146208][1217879]. All incidents resulted in hospital treatment or admission [2036538][1017209][1217879][2205704][1494319][2146208][2115614][1735357].

Arc flashes occur when workers contact energized equipment or when power is unintentionally restored while they are handling components, causing intense heat and burns to exposed skin and clothing [2287650][2132092][2309247][2203564][2168917][2171094][2277419][2161074]. In several cases the flash happened during maintenance, testing, or switching work on battery units, switchboards, panels, fuses, transformers, or furnace machinery, often after a circuit was unintentionally re‑energized or a protective barrier failed [2287650][2132092][2309247][2203564][2168917][2171094][2277419][2161074]. Lack of personal protective equipment or unexpected loss of power can increase exposure, leading to burns on the face, arms, hands, torso, or lower extremities [2287650][2132092][2309247][2203564][2168917][2171094][2277419][2161074].

In these reports, workers are injured when balers or trash compactors close or activate while a hand, arm, or leg is in the machine, causing crushing, fractures, or amputations [2224477][1327491][1344250][1006211]. Injuries also occur when a worker falls into a baler chute and the machine compacts, trapping and breaking or amputating limbs [2040030]. Activation of a compactor with failed anchor bolts can trap a worker between the equipment and a structure, resulting in severe pelvic injuries [963284]. Cleaning or maintenance activities near moving parts can lead to the equipment striking the worker, such as a conveyor falling onto a person cleaning a baler, causing multiple fractures and internal injuries [2094540].

In these reports, workers are injured when they climb onto or stand on a moving belt or its components and the belt is unintentionally restarted, pulling hands, fingers, arms, or the whole body into rollers or pulleys [971570][1408026][1878718][1919895]. Injuries also occur when workers attempt to clear jams, dislodge material, or clean the belt and the belt moves, pulling them under belts or pulleys and causing crushing injuries, fractures, or multiple traumatic injuries [1917941][1389723][1325674][2142122].

In these reports, workers were burned when hot oil splashed or spilled from fryers after an explosion or pressure‑release, such as a pressure fryer lid opening and ejecting grease [1176396] or a fryer exploding during use [1901818]. Workers also suffered burns after falling into or onto hot oil while cleaning, adjusting, or retrieving items, including slipping into a full fryer [1991684][1181719][1309577] or falling while pushing a fryer back into place, causing oil to spill onto the body [1018059]. Standing on active fryers to reach filters led to leg burns when the worker slipped and fell into the oil [1181719]. Lighting a propane‑fueled deep fryer caused a flash fire that burned the face and arms [2166303]. Direct contact with hot oil during cleaning resulted in hand burns [1156951].
In these reports, a worker who became engulfed in a grain bin was buried up to chest height and experienced breathing difficulties that required hospitalization [1488237].

In these reports, heat‑related hospitalizations occurred while an employee was operating an excursion press for a press saw in a metal‑working setting [1906877]. Hospitalizations also happened to workers delivering packages outdoors in high heat and humidity without cooling gear [2324395][2311839]. One case involved an employee working on molten aluminum production of sows [1498649]. Another employee was monitoring ladles in a foundry environment [1475021]. An apprentice lineman was hospitalized while working on utility line tasks [2092036]. Additional incidents described workers experiencing cramping or heat exhaustion during unspecified work in industrial facilities [2301479] and a general heat‑related illness during a shift in a maritime or related setting [1130403].

In these reports, workers who fall from ladders sustain serious injuries such as multiple fractures to the wrist, ribs, vertebrae, and limbs, as well as spinal fractures and internal injuries to the abdomen or chest [2229899][2112351][2156069][1176841][1230386][1239546][1222551][1516355]. Some falls result in head injuries, contusions, lacerations, or bruised lungs when the worker lands on their side or head [2156069]. Several incidents required hospitalization for broken bones, abdominal bleeding, or severe trauma to the spine and internal organs [2229899][1222551][1516355]. Injuries also include ankle, hip, and leg pain or soreness after landing on concrete surfaces [1239546].

In these reports, farm workers were injured when cattle or horses moved unexpectedly, stepped on, trampled, or struck them, often while herding, sorting, or transporting animals [1072088][1205258][1133223][2205109][1595137][1549072][1351793][1983218]. Injuries commonly included fractures to ribs, pelvis, hips, legs, or skull, as well as concussions, internal injuries, and facial lacerations or bruises [1072088][1205258][1133223][2205109][1595137][1549072][1351793][1983218]. The incidents occurred during activities such as moving cattle to a kill floor, driving cattle in a ring, sorting heifers, pushing cattle through gates, or riding a horse through a herd, indicating that loss of animal control can lead to severe blunt-force trauma [1072088][1205258][1133223][2205109][1595137][1549072][1351793][1983218].

In these reports, workers are injured by skid‑steer loaders when the machine tips or overturns, pinning or crushing limbs [1355280][983085]; when the loader moves unexpectedly, causing falls or trapping feet or ankles between parts [1896641][2018471][986311]; when a swinging bucket or other part strikes a person nearby [1440527]; and when a rider is thrown from the forks and then run over by the machine [1901366]; injuries also occur during maintenance if a worker falls from the cab or is struck by falling components [2220864].

In these reports, workers trapped by a trench collapse often suffer severe fractures to the ribs, spine, pelvis, femur, or other bones and may be pinned or engulfed up to their waist or higher [2223901][1852287][2282937][2208427][2152123][2193189][2328832][2240345]. Some workers are hospitalized for multiple broken bones and internal injuries, while others receive treatment without hospitalization if not as severely injured [2193189]. The collapse can also cause secondary impacts such as hitting rebar, concrete, or falling into adjacent openings, leading to additional wounds and dislocations [2152123][2328832].

In these reports, workers have been injured by wood chippers through impact from moving parts or debris, such as a wood slab striking a head and causing facial fractures and lacerations [1734715]. Workers have also had limbs caught in feed wheels, belts, or the drum, leading to amputations of fingers, toes, hands, forearms, or a leg up to the knee [1872241][2031134][1716652][1358674][1719905][1324665][1832891]. Some injuries occurred during routine feeding or cleaning, while others happened while repairing, testing, or performing housekeeping around the chipper, showing that both operational and maintenance activities can result in severe crushing or cutting injuries [1872241][2031134][1358674][1719905][1324665][1832891].

In these reports, workers who fall from aerial lifts often experience severe traumatic injuries such as multiple fractures, broken limbs, spinal injuries, head trauma, and internal organ damage [2321927][1495820][1855096][1553296][1833940][1892216][1038135][1164668]. The falls are typically caused by equipment failure, such as broken connection points, snapped boom pins, or collapse of the basket, or by external impacts from cranes, excavators, or overloaded loads striking the lift [2321927][1495820][1855096][1833940][1038135][1164668]. Falls can range from about 12 feet to over 140 feet, often resulting in hospitalization and, in some cases, life‑threatening injuries [1855096][1553296][1833940].

In these reports, workers are crushed or pinned by the vehicle when it overturns, leading to broken or fractured legs and feet [1094696][1460625][2198316]. When the ATV rolls onto its side, occupants can strike interior components such as the steering wheel, causing head lacerations, broken collarbones, and multiple rib fractures [2255033]. Rollovers that eject the rider result in spinal injuries, such as a fractured C6 vertebra [2319631]. If a roll bar breaks loose during a flip, it can strike the back, producing broken ribs and internal organ damage like a lacerated liver [2189881]. Other rollovers cause head lacerations and multiple fractures from impact with the vehicle or ground [1147407].

In these reports, workers are injured when their hands or fingers are pulled into the moving blade while trying to clear material, set up the machine, or hold objects near the blade [1922517][1551287][968491][1894212]. Hands are also caught by hydraulic vises, feeder mechanisms, or wheel‑blade interfaces, leading to amputations, fractures, or crush injuries [1551287][1039625][1105589][1218588]. Gloves or other items can be drawn into the blade, causing lacerations or wrist cuts [1363881][968491].

In these reports, workers were cut when glass panels or sheets broke while being removed, carried, or placed, causing shards to strike limbs such as the arm, forearm, leg, hand, or neck [1256645][1769562][1771563][1111496][1500979][1457438][2033131]. Cuts also occurred when glass slipped from a hand or fell from a crate, striking the worker directly [1769562][1160792]. Handling large broken pieces that shattered during transport to a dumpster or hopper also produced severe lacerations [1771563][1457438].

In these reports, workers are injured when a chainsaw kicks back or is lost‑control, causing the blade to strike the operator’s body parts such as fingers, hand, knee, thigh, or face [1195856][1331802][2219740][1956195][1714741][1410513][1195162][1518844]. Injuries are described as cuts, lacerations, and punctures, often requiring hospitalization and surgery [1195856][1331802][2219740][1956195][1714741][1410513][1195162][1518844]. Lack of personal protective equipment is noted in at least one case, increasing the severity of the laceration [1331802].

In these reports, chemicals that splash into a worker’s eyes cause immediate eye injuries such as swelling, inflammation, irritation, pain, and chemical burns or corrosions [1419275][1896815][2313834][1883036][1752838][1890408][1451649][1030967]. Several incidents required medical treatment, with some workers being hospitalized for the eye injuries [1419275][2313834][1752838][1030967].

In these reports, pedestrians walking in aisles or near racks were struck by forklifts that were moving forward, backing up, or bouncing over a bump, causing the vehicle’s wheels or a load to run over their feet [1440509][1978965][1356746][2045712][1010605][1170967]. Injuries described include crushing of the foot or ankle, fractures of toes, foot bones, or the heel, and in one case a load falling onto a boot and pinning it to the ground, resulting in multiple foot fractures [2112602]. The incidents occurred while employees were walking, standing, or assisting with tasks near the forklift’s path, and the injuries resulted from direct contact with wheels, counterweights, or falling loads [1440509][1978965][1356746][2112602][2045712][1010605][1170967].

In these reports, roofers are burned when hot tar or asphalt spills or splashes onto them after a loss of balance, a fall, or a sudden release from equipment such as a bucket, hose, pipe, or mop cart [2032518][1387993][1157791][1226638][1381295][1458262]. The hot material can be released when a hose connection comes off, a pipe bursts, a pipe or pipe‑line leaks, or a bucket is grabbed for balance, causing the liquid to spray or splash onto the worker’s skin, face, arms, hands, or forearms [2151059][2336122][1458262]. Workers often sustain burns ranging from first‑degree to third‑degree, depending on the temperature of the tar or asphalt and the extent of contact [1157791][1226638][1458262].

Workers are scalded when hot water is unexpectedly released or sprayed onto them, such as when a valve is opened and water discharges onto a standing employee [1488801]. They can be burned while positioned under equipment that ejects hot water, like a case washing machine [1737512]. Opening the lid of a container or clarifier can cause hot water to spill onto the worker’s body [1769083]. Over‑pressurized lines may burst, spraying scalding water onto the employee’s exposed areas [1238742]. Filling containers or tanks with hot water can result in the water striking the worker’s feet, ankles, or back during the task [1521189][1016725]. Cleaning operations can cause hot water to back‑flow or be released from pipes or transfer belts, scalding the employee during scale removal or belt cleaning [1147154][1345571].

In these reports, workers who slipped on ice sustained head injuries, including a hospitalized concussion [2124148]. Several reports describe fractures to major bones such as the hip, shoulder, femur, pelvic bone, rib, and leg(s) [1420261][2248654][2259127][967926]. Knee, tibia, and other leg injuries requiring surgery or hospitalization are also noted [2122022][2118003][964841]. Internal injuries such as a lung contusion were reported alongside rib fractures [2259127].

In these reports, woodworkers are injured when their hands or fingers contact the moving cutters of a jointer, resulting in amputations or severe lacerations of fingers [1377019][1879915][1829445][1265496][2333914]. In one case a push‑stick was used but the worker’s guiding hand reached the blade, causing multiple finger losses [1265496]. Another incident involved the workpiece jumping and forcing the hand into the cutter head, producing partial amputations [2333914]. These injuries occur during normal feeding or trimming of wood on the jointer.

In these reports, workers were caught when a hand or body part was pulled between a rotating shaft and a polishing or emery cloth attached to the lathe [1508380][1270853]. A lanyard around a worker’s neck became entangled in the lathe, pulling the worker into the machine [1534685]. A loose workpiece or part being turned came free and struck the worker’s hand or was grabbed, pulling the hand into the machine [1315154][1194993]. The lead screw or tailstock caught a shirt or clothing, drawing the worker toward the moving parts [2042582]. A bar being machined struck the worker directly, causing injury [1383548].

In these reports, a worker using a hydraulic splitter was injured when a log fell and crushed the hand against a metal part of the machine, resulting in finger amputation [1963406]. Another worker was injured while adjusting a log in the splitter, causing a fingertip amputation [993865]. A third worker held a log on top of a vertical splitter; when the foot pedal was pressed the blades descended and amputated part of his index finger [1337934].

In these reports, workers using meat slicers suffered amputations of fingers or fingertips, often from the blade contacting a hand, finger, thumb, or fingertip while slicing, cleaning, or adjusting the equipment [1873773][1053999][1933213][1717341][1286634][1235785][2012939][1466000].

In these reports, workers are injured when a dough hook, blade, or rotating part catches an arm, hand, or finger while the mixer is running, often while checking dough texture or size [2021995][2293515]. Injuries also occur when a worker reaches into the bowl or tries to retrieve a dropped tool, causing fingers or hands to be crushed, lacerated, or fractured by the moving mixers or rollers [976178][1734496]. Cleaning or maintenance activities without lockout can lead to hands being caught between moving components, resulting in fractures or amputations [1291880][1860006]. Even while squatting to inspect a mixer, loss of balance can cause a worker to grab machinery and have a finger crushed [2024500].

In these reports, workers’ feet are injured when a pallet‑jack wheel rolls over or runs into the foot, often after the jack becomes unstuck, is backed up, or continues moving unintentionally, causing lacerations, crushing, or fractures to toes and other foot structures [1484843][2149407][2355177][1090866][1540148][1462025][1521561][1087906].

In these reports, healthcare workers were physically assaulted by patients, resulting in a range of injuries such as concussions, loss of consciousness, facial and head lacerations, fractures, internal injuries, burns, and musculoskeletal strains [2324604][2231828][1243368][1318890][1580729][1420434][2355581]. Some incidents occurred while providing direct medical care, while others happened during custodial tasks or when restraining a combative patient, leading to severe outcomes including hospitalization and, in one case, a possible heart attack [1274566][2324604][2231828]. The assaults involved kicking, punching, shoving, throwing objects, and other violent actions by the patients.

In these reports, printing press operators are injured when hands or fingers are pulled into moving rollers, pinch points, or other moving parts of the press during normal operation or while loading, unloading, or cleaning paper or plates, resulting in crushing, crushing‑type amputations, or severe hand injuries such as degloving and nerve or tendon damage [1828543][1804384][2111803][1832205][1178893][2130025].

In these reports, farm workers were injured when their bodies or clothing became caught in a rotating PTO shaft, pulling them into the moving part and causing fractures, lacerations, or contusions [2270329][2093017][1448171]. One worker’s shirt was drawn into the shaft while walking near a tractor, resulting in severe arm lacerations [2093017]. Another worker stepped over the PTO, and his pants snagged on the shaft, pulling him into the rotating mechanism and breaking a thumb and bruising his legs [1448171]. A third worker was entangled in the PTO and associated hydraulic hoses while operating a manure pump, leading to multiple fractures and other injuries [2270329].

In these reports, employees are physically assaulted by robbers or shoplifters who push, shove, or strike them, often causing head injuries such as contusions, fractures, skull or brain trauma, and facial injuries [2111468][2225194][1406445][1518874][1290328][2353293][1007273]. Some incidents involve the employee being forced to the ground or onto hard surfaces, resulting in pelvic fractures or rib fractures [1406445][2353293]. Assaults can also occur after the employee pursues a suspect outside the store, leading to additional blows to the face and head in parking areas [2225194][1007273].

In these reports, workers who fall off roofs sustain severe injuries such as multiple fractures, broken legs, and internal organ damage [1826124][2213065]. They also experience serious head trauma including brain bleeds, skull and orbital fractures, loss of vision, and concussions [2223266][1969166][1595467][2137097]. Additional injuries reported include broken ribs, collapsed sinuses, loss of an eye, and severe wounds to the trunk and extremities [2325920][1313337]. Many of the incidents required hospitalization and resulted in extensive medical treatment [1826124][2213065][2223266][1595467].

In these reports, workers who fall down stairs often sustain serious injuries such as head trauma, fractures, rib or chest injuries, and lacerations, and they are typically hospitalized for treatment [2325968][1069032][1965060][2259006][2350421][1643254][1139385][2339013].

In these reports, workers exposed to escaping steam suffered thermal burns ranging from partial‑thickness to third‑degree on exposed skin such as arms, face, torso, back, buttocks, and extremities [2202148][1341401][2304726][1543725][1737060][2135416][2059393]. Some incidents also involved additional injuries like fractures when steam was released under pressure [1341401]. Several exposures occurred when steam was released from equipment failures, open flanges, or unsecured hoses during maintenance, inspection, or cleaning activities [2304726][1737060][2059393]. The injuries were severe enough to require hospitalization for at least one worker in each incident, with one case involving burns to about half the body [981859][2059393].

The minimization masked full employer names but not shortened forms; about 74-101 of 105,996 narratives still contain part of their employer's name (local count). Deployment stays blocked until masking is strengthened.

All 4 in-domain adversarial prompts scored above the threshold; the model declined each.
